scope: Five complete source reviews: three larger endgame analyses and two opening/middlegame reviews outside endgame-study scope. No unverified composition promoted. Original v3 unchanged.

_pyRnT3cHCk.notes: All 49 saved states and narration reviewed. A follower-game review progresses from a Fried Liver opening error through queen exchanges into a genuine material-deficit ending. The source teaches avoiding unnecessary exchanges when down material, then shows further trades, Black’s promotion and abandonment. Complete diagrams are available, but the relevant ending remains larger than seven pieces.
_pyRnT3cHCk.analysis_required: Reconstruct the actual queenless ending before the final pawn promotion and distinguish it from the earlier hypothetical queen-exchange sidelines. Check the source’s simplification advice in the concrete position, retaining both kings, both rooks where present, Black’s bishops and every spare pawn. Verify the actual rook-trade/king-activation/promotion sequence with larger-position analysis before claiming forced wins; the source’s general principle is not an exact outcome proof.

fUAHZTTvVHw.notes: All 66 saved states and captions reviewed. This follower-game review is an opening/middlegame lesson about the central ...e4 trap, f3 weakening, counting attackers and missing ...Qf2 mate. The clip ends in that early queen/knight attack with many pieces and pawns still present. There is no worked endgame setup or conversion. Retained in the searchable channel archive rather than the endgame-study queue.

F-RxuNseei8.notes: All 72 saved states and narration reviewed. London-game advice centers on an overloaded queen defending the backward e-pawn, Rh7?, exchanges on h7 and a middlegame king hunt ending in mate. The outside-passer/endgame references are hypothetical advice and the closing recommendation is to study endgames; neither supplies a worked endgame conversion. Many major/minor pieces and pawns remain in the illustrated finish. Retained as a searchable game review outside endgame-study scope.

DGEGLAql0As.notes: All 40 saved states and narration reviewed. Complete nine-piece starting diagram: White Kb8/Ba8/b7/d7/f7/h7 against Black Kb5/Bg5/Rf1, Black to move. The full checking shepherd sequence and final ...Ka6 waiting idea are visible; all four promotion-ready white pawns remain significant.
DGEGLAql0As.analysis_required: Verify the full nine-piece ...Bf4+ king shepherd with every legal White reply, the return trip induced by ...Bg7+, and the final ...Ka6/promote/Ba7 mating idea. Preserve White’s Ba8 and all four seventh-rank pawns: promotion interpositions are the defense to the premature bishop maneuver. The source labels selected checks as forced, but legality and outcome of every encoded intermediate diagram still require larger-position proof. Do not drop pawns to fit tablebase coverage or present the final mate alone as verification of the whole plan.

cjgp5RYMyfQ.notes: All 71 saved states and narration reviewed. The complete source shows Qf8 sacrifice, knight rerouting under rook-mate threats, g-pawn blockade and a long king/pawn zugzwang conversion. Numerous spare pawns remain throughout, including after promotion. Source evidence is available.
cjgp5RYMyfQ.analysis_required: Reconstruct the complete larger setup and check the direct queen capture/stalemate trap against Qf8/Rxf8/Nf2. Verify Nh3/Nf4/Kb1/Nh5/Nf6 timing, the ...Rxf6/d8=Q+/Rxd8/g7 blockade, then king capture of the mobile pawns and the b-pawn sacrifice that releases a7. Distinguish the illustrated king/rook replies from all legal defenses and use supported larger-position analysis; even the final queen/pawn position retains more than seven pieces.
